title: 1 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 22.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: David escaped to the cave Adullam
David went to Mizpeh of Moab
Saul heard that David was discovered
The prophet Gad said to David to depart to the land of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: David escaped to the cave Adullam
questions.explanation: David's departure and escape to the cave Adullam is described at the very start of the chapter in 1 Samuel 22:1.

questions.question: Where did David escape to according to 1 Samuel 22?
questions.correctAnswer: The cave Adullam
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:1 states that David escaped to the cave Adullam.

questions.question: Who gathered themselves unto David at the cave Adullam?
options: Everyone in distress, in debt, and discontented
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone in distress, in debt, and discontented
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:2 explains that everyone in distress, in debt, and discontented gathered unto David.

questions.question: Approximately how many men were with David as their captain?
questions.correctAnswer: About four hundred
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:2 states that there were about four hundred men with David.

questions.question: To whom did David go after the cave Adullam?
questions.correctAnswer: Mizpeh of Moab
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:3 states that David went to Mizpeh of Moab after the cave Adullam.

questions.question: What did David ask the king of Moab regarding his parents?
options: To let them stay with him until David knew what God would do
To send them back to Israel immediately
questions.correctAnswer: To let them stay with him until David knew what God would do
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:3 shows David asking the king of Moab to let his father and mother stay with him until he knew what God would do.

questions.question: Who advised David to leave the hold and go into the land of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: The prophet Gad
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:5 states that the prophet Gad told David to depart from the hold and go into the land of Judah.

questions.question: Where did David go after departing from the hold as advised?
questions.correctAnswer: The forest of Hareth
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:5 mentions that David came into the forest of Hareth after leaving the hold.

questions.question: Where was Saul when he heard that David was discovered?
options: Gibeah under a tree in Ramah
questions.correctAnswer: Gibeah under a tree in Ramah
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:6 states that Saul was in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah when he heard that David was discovered.

questions.question: What was Saul holding as he sat under the tree in Ramah?
questions.correctAnswer: His spear
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:6 describes Saul as having his spear in his hand while sitting under the tree.

questions.question: What did Saul ask the Benjamite servants about David, the son of Jesse?
options: If David would give them fields, vineyards, and captaincies
If David was loyal to Saul
If David was hiding in the forest
If David had fled to Moab
questions.correctAnswer: If David would give them fields, vineyards, and captaincies
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:7 shows Saul asking if David would give them fields, vineyards, and make them captains.

questions.question: What did Saul accuse the Benjamites of in his speech?
options: Conspiring against him and not informing him about David's actions
questions.correctAnswer: Conspiring against him and not informing him about David's actions
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:8 shows Saul accusing the Benjamites of conspiring against him and not showing him that David made a league against him.

questions.question: David became a captain over about four hundred men who were in distress, debt, and discontented.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:2 states that David became a captain over about four hundred men who were in distress, in debt, and discontented.

questions.question: David asked the king of Moab to protect his parents while he sought God's guidance.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:3-4 shows David asking the king of Moab to allow his parents to stay with him until he knew what God would do.

questions.question: Saul was in Mizpeh of Moab when he heard that David was discovered.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:6 states that Saul was in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah, not Mizpeh of Moab.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who reported David's visit to Ahimelech the priest at Nob to King Saul?
questions.correctAnswer: Doeg the Edomite
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:9 states that Doeg the Edomite answered and said he saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob to Ahimelech.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 22:16 promise will happen if someone conspires against King Saul like Ahimelech did, according to 1 Samuel 22:13?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall surely die
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:13 accuses Ahimelech of conspiring with David against Saul, and 1 Samuel 22:16 declares that Ahimelech and all his father's house shall surely die.

questions.question: What items did Ahimelech give David when he enquired of the LORD for him?
options: Victuals and the sword of Goliath
questions.correctAnswer: Victuals and the sword of Goliath
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:10 states Ahimelech gave David victuals and the sword of Goliath the Philistine.

questions.question: How did Ahimelech respond when Saul accused him of conspiring with David?
options: He denied knowledge and claimed innocence
questions.correctAnswer: He denied knowledge and claimed innocence
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:15 shows Ahimelech telling Saul that he knew nothing of the conspiracy and beseeches the king not to impute guilt to him or his father's house.

questions.question: What qualities did Ahimelech attribute to David when defending him before Saul?
options: Faithfulness, son-in-law of the king, honorable
A stranger to the king's house
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness, son-in-law of the king, honorable
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 22:14, Ahimelech states David is the most faithful among Saul's servants, the king's son-in-law, and honorable in Saul's house.

questions.question: What was David's situation when he gathered about four hundred men to him?
options: They were distressed, in debt, and discontented
questions.correctAnswer: They were distressed, in debt, and discontented
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:2 describes that those who were in distress, debt, and discontent gathered to David, making him captain over them.

questions.question: Where did David go to bring his father and mother for safety?
questions.correctAnswer: Mizpeh of Moab
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:3 records David going to Mizpeh of Moab and asking the king to shelter his parents.

questions.question: What instruction did the prophet Gad give David after his stay in the hold?
options: Abide not in the hold; depart and get into the land of Judah
Remain hidden in the hold indefinitely
Go to Philistine territory for safety
questions.correctAnswer: Abide not in the hold; depart and get into the land of Judah
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:5 shows the prophet Gad instructing David not to stay in the hold but to depart and go to Judah.

questions.question: How did Saul react when he heard David was discovered with his men?
options: He was in Gibeah under a tree with his spear in hand, surrounded by servants
He immediately went to parley with David
He fled the city in fear
He sent gifts to David's men
questions.correctAnswer: He was in Gibeah under a tree with his spear in hand, surrounded by servants
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:6 describes Saul's posture and location when he learned of David's presence.

questions.question: What did Saul accuse the Benjamite servants of in his speech?
options: Conspiring against him by supporting David
questions.correctAnswer: Conspiring against him by supporting David
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:7-8 records Saul accusing his servants of conspiring and not showing sorrow for him concerning David.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Saul and Ahimelech teach about integrity and truthfulness in difficult situations?
options: Integrity requires standing firm in truth even when accused falsely
It is better to confess to wrongdoing even if innocent
Avoid answering difficult questions to stay safe
Always agree with authority to avoid conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity requires standing firm in truth even when accused falsely
questions.explanation: Ahimelech's response in 1 Samuel 22:15 shows he defended his innocence despite Saul's accusations, demonstrating integrity.

questions.question: How might David's act of seeking the LORD through Ahimelech encourage Christians in times of distress?
options: It shows the importance of seeking God's guidance and provision
It suggests avoiding prayer and relying on self
It implies leaders should not trust priests
It teaches hiding from God in caves
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of seeking God's guidance and provision
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:10 highlights David enquiring of the LORD through Ahimelech, emphasizing prayer and reliance on God.

questions.question: What practical lesson about loyalty and faithfulness can be learned from Ahimelech's defense of David?
options: Loyalty to faithful servants is a virtue to uphold
Loyalty should be given only to kings
Faithfulness is irrelevant in times of conflict
Accusing others is the best way to protect oneself
questions.correctAnswer: Loyalty to faithful servants is a virtue to uphold
questions.explanation: Ahimelech praises David's faithfulness in 1 Samuel 22:14, teaching the value of loyalty to trustworthy individuals.

questions.question: True or False: Saul immediately believed Ahimelech's explanation and spared him and his family.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:16 shows Saul ordering the death of Ahimelech and all his father's house despite Ahimelech's defense.

questions.question: True or False: David gathered about four hundred men who were in distress, debt, and discontent to follow him at the cave of Adullam.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:1-2 explains David gathered those who were distressed, in debt, and discontented, numbering about four hundred.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 22.

questions.question: Who did King Saul command to slay the priests of the LORD in 1 Samuel 22:17?
options: The footmen that stood about him
questions.correctAnswer: The footmen that stood about him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:17 states that the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, 'Turn, and slay the priests of the LORD.'

questions.question: Why did Saul order the slaying of the priests according to 1 Samuel 22:17?
options: Because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me
Because they refused to give him food
questions.correctAnswer: Because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me
questions.explanation: The verse 1 Samuel 22:17 explicitly records Saul's reason: 'because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me.'

questions.question: Who actually carried out the killing of the priests when Saul's servants refused in 1 Samuel 22:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Doeg the Edomite
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:18 states that Doeg the Edomite turned and slew the priests when the servants would not.

questions.question: How many priests did Doeg the Edomite kill in 1 Samuel 22:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Eighty-five
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:18 specifies that Doeg killed 'fourscore and five persons,' which is eighty-five.

questions.question: What city, described as the city of the priests, was destroyed by Doeg in 1 Samuel 22:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Nob
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:19 states that Nob, the city of the priests, was smitten by Doeg.

questions.question: Who escaped the massacre at Nob and fled to David according to 1 Samuel 22:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Abiathar, son of Ahimelech
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:20 identifies Abiathar, son of Ahimelech, as the one who escaped and fled to David.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ephod' in 1 Samuel 22:18 refer to?
questions.correctAnswer: A priestly garment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ephod' refers to a linen priestly garment worn by the priests, as used in 1 Samuel 22:18 describing those slain.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Samuel 22:17-19 to emphasize the severity of Saul's command and its execution?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: These verses form a chiasm emphasizing Saul's order, the servants' refusal, Doeg's action, and the destruction of Nob, centering on the tragic killing (1 Samuel 22:17-19).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of innocent persecution as seen in 1 Samuel 22:17-19?
options: Matthew 5:10 - 'Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake'
John 3:16 - 'For God so loved the world'
Romans 8:28 - 'All things work together for good'
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 5:10 - 'Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake'
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:10 connects with 1 Samuel 22:17-19 by addressing persecution of the righteous, similar to the priests slain for aiding David.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage foreshadows the massacre of the priests in 1 Samuel 22:17-19?
options: Exodus 12:29 - The death of the firstborn in Egypt
Leviticus 10:1-2 - The death of Nadab and Abihu
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 10:1-2 - The death of Nadab and Abihu
questions.explanation: Leviticus 10:1-2 foreshadows priestly death due to disobedience or association with sin, paralleling the priests' fate in 1 Samuel 22:17-19.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Saul commanding the death of the priests in 1 Samuel 22:17?
options: Doeg reports David's visit to Ahimelech
David escapes to the cave of Adullam
David sends his parents to Moab
Gad instructs David to leave the hold
questions.correctAnswer: Doeg reports David's visit to Ahimelech
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:9-10 records Doeg informing Saul about David's visit to Ahimelech, directly preceding the king's deadly command in verse 17.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 22:22, David expresses a realization about Doeg's presence. What literary device does this reflect?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: David's statement in 1 Samuel 22:22 foreshadows the tragic outcome resulting from Doeg's betrayal.

questions.question: How does Abiathar's escape in 1 Samuel 22:20 contribute to the narrative's typology?
options: He becomes a priestly ally and advisor to David, prefiguring the New Testament priesthood
He leads a rebellion against Saul
questions.correctAnswer: He becomes a priestly ally and advisor to David, prefiguring the New Testament priesthood
questions.explanation: Abiathar’s escape and alliance with David (1 Samuel 22:20) typologically prefigures the priestly support in the New Testament, such as Christ’s high priesthood.

questions.question: What theological theme is highlighted by the refusal of Saul’s servants to kill the priests in 1 Samuel 22:17?
options: Respect for the sanctity of the priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for the sanctity of the priesthood
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:17 shows Saul's servants refusing to harm the priests, demonstrating respect for their sacred office despite the king's orders.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Samuel 22:23, David promises Abiathar safety with him because their lives are linked.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:23 records David telling Abiathar, 'for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard,' promising protection.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Samuel 22:2 teach about God’s providential care in times of human distress?
options: God sovereignly provides refuge and leadership for the distressed
God abandons the discontented to their own devices
God punishes those in debt by exclusion
God primarily judges through public humiliation
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly provides refuge and leadership for the distressed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 22:2 shows that those in distress, debt, and discontent gathered to David, indicating God's providential care in raising a leader as refuge and captain for them.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding divine guidance and prophetic counsel is taught in 1 Samuel 22:5?
options: God directs His people through prophetic instruction to ensure their safety
Prophetic counsel is optional and often ignored without consequence
God’s guidance is only accessible through kings, not prophets
Prophets primarily serve to predict political events rather than guide individuals
questions.correctAnswer: God directs His people through prophetic instruction to ensure their safety
questions.explanation: Verse 22:5 records the prophet Gad instructing David to leave the hold and go to Judah, demonstrating the doctrine that God guides His people through prophets for their protection and leading.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin and responsibility is conveyed in 1 Samuel 22:16 regarding Saul’s actions?
options: The sinful exercise of royal authority leads to unjust execution and guilt
Kings are not accountable for their orders if they claim divine sanction
Murder committed by government officials is exempt from moral judgment
The death penalty is always justified for priests who aid enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The sinful exercise of royal authority leads to unjust execution and guilt
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 22:16, Saul orders the death of Ahimelech and all his father’s house, illustrating the doctrine that misuse of authority through sin results in wrongful judgment and moral guilt.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Samuel 22:10 specifically demonstrate by David’s receiving of the sword of Goliath and divine provision?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Verse 22:10 reveals God’s sovereign provision through Ahimelech, giving David bread and the sword of Goliath, showing God’s control over events and resources.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 1 Samuel 22:23 where David assures Abiathar of safety despite Saul’s pursuit?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: David’s promise in 22:23 to protect Abiathar reflects the attribute of faithfulness, God’s covenantal loyalty mirrored in David’s care.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 22 connect to the broader biblical theme of God raising a deliverer for the oppressed?
options: David’s gathering of the marginalized prefigures the Messiah’s mission to the lost
It shows the failure of human kingship apart from divine election
It emphasizes Israel’s rejection of God’s prophets
It demonstrates God’s preference for monarchy over judges
questions.correctAnswer: David’s gathering of the marginalized prefigures the Messiah’s mission to the lost
questions.explanation: David’s leadership of the distressed and discontented in 22:2 anticipates the Messiah’s role as one who seeks and saves the lost (cf. Luke 19:10).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme is prepared by the massacre of the priests in 1 Samuel 22:18-19?
options: The gravity of apostasy and the cost of covenant unfaithfulness
The inevitability of human sacrifice in Israel’s worship
The triumph of Saul’s dynasty as divinely ordained
God’s approval of violent purges for national unity
questions.correctAnswer: The gravity of apostasy and the cost of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: The slaughter of priests in these verses underscores the consequences of rejecting God’s covenant and leadership, foreshadowing later judgments on apostasy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Samuel 22:7 and 1 Samuel 22:8 teach about human sin and leadership?
options: Human pride and conspiracy against God’s anointed leader result in broken relationships and divine judgment
Kings are justified in punishing any perceived disloyalty without evidence
Human leaders are infallible and above reproach in their accusations
The people’s loyalty is primarily to political power, not to God’s chosen
questions.correctAnswer: Human pride and conspiracy against God’s anointed leader result in broken relationships and divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 show Saul accusing the Benjamites of conspiring with David, illustrating sinful pride and betrayal that damage God-ordained leadership and provoke judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and human complicity is taught by combining 1 Samuel 22:17 and 1 Samuel 22:18?
options: God permits human agents to carry out judgment, but human evil multiplies when servants refuse to obey God’s moral standards
Human agents always act righteously when executing divine justice
God directly commands all acts of violence without human responsibility
The refusal of servants to act always leads to divine punishment
questions.correctAnswer: God permits human agents to carry out judgment, but human evil multiplies when servants refuse to obey God’s moral standards
questions.explanation: In 22:17 servants refuse to kill priests, but Doeg obeys Saul’s sinful command, showing how human complicity in evil contrasts with God’s justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about faithfulness and divine protection is taught by 1 Samuel 22:20 and 1 Samuel 22:23?
options: God preserves the faithful remnant and provides protection through covenant community
Faithfulness leads inevitably to martyrdom without divine rescue
Human safety depends solely on political power, not divine care
Divine protection is guaranteed only to kings, not priests
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves the faithful remnant and provides protection through covenant community
questions.explanation: Abiathar’s escape (22:20) and David’s promise to protect him (22:23) illustrate God’s preservation of the faithful remnant within His covenant people.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 Samuel 22:17-19 condones religious violence and murder committed by Saul. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It portrays Saul’s actions negatively and shows the servants’ refusal to kill priests as righteous
It endorses Saul’s massacre as divinely sanctioned and morally required
It suggests all violence against enemies of the king is justified
It shows God commanding Saul to kill innocent priests
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays Saul’s actions negatively and shows the servants’ refusal to kill priests as righteous
questions.explanation: The text in 22:17-19 indicates the servants’ refusal to carry out Saul’s command, implying disapproval of Saul’s sinful orders rather than endorsement.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Samuel 22:1 teach about God’s providence in the formation of a godly community?
options: God providentially gathers the family and kinship network around His chosen leader
God calls only isolated individuals without social ties
God’s providence excludes family in the calling of leaders
God’s people must always separate from their families to follow Him
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially gathers the family and kinship network around His chosen leader
questions.explanation: Verse 22:1 describes David’s family and relatives coming to him, showing God’s providential formation of a community around His anointed.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 1 Samuel 22:6 when Saul is depicted holding his spear and surrounded by servants?
questions.correctAnswer: Wrath
questions.explanation: Saul’s posture and readiness for violence in 22:6 reflect God permitting the manifestation of human wrath through Saul’s spirit.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 22:11-13 contribute to the theological understanding of the relationship between priests and kings?
options: Priests serve God’s purposes and may act independently of royal suspicion
Priests are always subordinate to kings and must obey all royal commands unconditionally
Kings have divine authority over priests in all matters
Priests only serve political interests without spiritual responsibilities
questions.correctAnswer: Priests serve God’s purposes and may act independently of royal suspicion
questions.explanation: Ahimelech’s response in 22:14-15 shows priests acting faithfully toward David despite Saul’s accusations, reflecting their spiritual role distinct from kingship.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 22:3-4 teach about the role of intercession and hospitality in divine providence?
options: God’s providence includes the protection of family through the hospitality of foreign kings
Intercession and hospitality are irrelevant to God’s plan
God’s protection is only national, not extended to foreigners
Foreign kings never cooperate with God’s anointed
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence includes the protection of family through the hospitality of foreign kings
questions.explanation: David’s request and the Moabite king’s hospitality in 22:3-4 show God’s providential use of foreign rulers to protect His people.
